kind_note: A standard gen_configs.py / run_experiments.py / merge_experiments.py repair campaign over the TLSF corpus, so its rows share the schema of the other repair campaigns and merge_experiments.py reads it. One thing is unusual: every emitted repair was re-checked outside the run that produced it, by a checker script vendored here beside the drivers. That verdict file has no counterpart in any earlier campaign.
question: Whether the *well-separation* filter should run every generation or once at the end, the way the weakening filter can be throttled. Cadence is the only factor. The accept/reject predicate is identical in all three arms, so the comparison is search quality and cost against schedule. The 2026-07-23 wellsep campaign settled whether to run the filter at all and said nothing about when; no campaign before this one varied the cadence.
decision: Final-only is rejected. It is not a cheaper end-of-run screen, it is no screen at all: its leak rate of 0.427 sits within a few points of the unfiltered control's 0.441 on all sixteen specs. `run_well_separation` and `allow_output_assumptions` both flip to true as C++ defaults in the commit that adds this directory, with `well_separation_interval` staying at 1. The two defaults move together because `allow_output_assumptions` on without the filter is the configuration EXPERIMENTS.md:416 records as a false-positive machine, lifting found_repair from 0.80 to 1.00 on repairs the filter would reject. All three arms here state both keys explicitly, so this campaign is immune to that default flip.

profile_commit.subject: feat(experiments): size the wellsep-timing grid from calibration

profile_commit_evidence: Not inferred from any mtime. `counter --version` was captured into each host's manifest at startup and reads commit=cbcaede, dirty=0 for both the counter and compare binaries on both hosts, and all 7200 CSV rows carry commit=cbcaede, dirty=0. At the time of archiving cbcaede is not an ancestor of main and is held only by the branch; it becomes reachable when feat/wellsep-timing merges, and no provenance/ tag is needed for that path. If the branch is instead split into reconstructed pull requests, the same content reaches main under fresh shas while this one stops resolving, and an annotated tag has to be cut before the branch is deleted. That is exactly the position 2026-07-31-replicate ended in, which is why provenance/replicate-campaign exists.
binary_commit_note: Same commit as the profile, recorded the same way and from the same evidence: the per-host manifests and every row's commit column. Both binaries were built clean, dirty=0 on both hosts.

run_window.note: Local time, +0100. av3's CSV holds 3600 rows against 3588 launched: 12 rows already existed from the pre-launch smoke test and the resume key skipped them. Those 12 carry the same commit and dirty=0 as the campaign proper, so they are not distinguishable from campaign rows and are not excluded. av3's historical clock skew of about 17 min is not corrected for and does not matter, because no figure here derives from a cross-host timestamp.

nofilter.role: control. Bounds what the filter costs and what it removes.

every-gen.role: the shipped behaviour when the filter was enabled.

final-only.role: treatment. Needs no code change: both drivers force every per-generation filter on the last generation whatever its interval (`filters_for_generation` in src/genetic/generation.cpp, `select_active_filters` in src/tlsf/pipeline.cpp), so an interval above the generation count leaves exactly that one forced pass.

arms.shared: allow_output_assumptions = true, generations = 10, population_size = 200, selection_scheme = "nsga2", crossover_rate 0.1, mutation_rate 1.0, metric "direct", default_bound 20, repair_mode "monolithic", black_timeout_ms 1000, ltlsynt_timeout_ms 500, ltl2tgba_timeout_ms 60000, max_scoring_failure_rate 0.15, run_weakening and run_implication true.
arms.why_output_assumptions_is_fixed: allow_output_assumptions is held on rather than crossed because the 2026-07-23 wellsep campaign measured the filter completely inert with input-only assumptions. Input-only assumptions are well-separated by construction, so there is nothing to reject, and timing an inert filter measures nothing.

grid.shape: 16 TLSF specs x 150 seeds x 3 arms = 7200 runs. All present, 0 errors on either host.
grid.specs: arbiter, arbiter-aurus, arbiter-handshake, codesample-un1, codesample-un2, detector, gyro-var1, gyro-var2, humanoid-458, lift, lily02, load-balancer, minepump, rg1, rg2, round-robin-arbiter
grid.hosts: Seeds 0-74 on av3, 75-149 on av2. Disjoint and seed-major, so a deadline kill would have left a balanced design.
grid.exclusions: Five specs excluded on cost -- amba, full-arbiter, humanoid-531, prioritized-arbiter and simple-arbiter each exceeded 90 s on a single seed under the expensive arm. takeoff-tlsf is excluded for having no ideal fix under examples/<spec>/fixes, which would leave implies_ideal undefined on part of the grid.

leak_check_method: Every emitted repair_*.tlsf on all three arms was re-checked outside the run that produced it, by check_well_separated.py calling ltlsynt directly with no cache, one call per file. 33998 repairs checked, 0 undecided, so no verdict rests on a checker timeout. A run cannot be its own witness on whether its output is well-separated, which is why this is measured rather than assumed.

results.headline: Per arm: leak rate / found_repair / implies_ideal / mean n_repairs / mean wall s / median paired wall ratio against nofilter / run timeouts. nofilter 0.441 / 0.999 / 0.315 / 5.15 / 12.23 / 1.000 / 2. every-gen 0.000 (1 leak in 9529) / 0.899 / 0.355 / 3.97 / 11.27 / 0.949 / 0. final-only 0.427 / 0.999 / 0.317 / 5.05 / 11.89 / 0.991 / 2. Wall ratios are paired on (spec, seed), n = 2400 each, sign test p = 8.93e-38 for every-gen and p = 1.70e-16 for final-only. 4 run timeouts in 7200, so nothing is censored and the failure mode section 7 of PLAN.md guards against did not occur.
results.result_1_final_only_is_inert: The forced last-generation pass does run -- a filter report from a final-only arbiter run reads `not-well-separated  25 in  17 out  32.0% avg drop` -- but its drops never reach the output. Per spec, final-only's leak tracks the unfiltered control within a few points on all sixteen: arbiter 0.891 against 0.905, arbiter-aurus 0.479 against 0.501, codesample-un2 0.819 against 0.826, rg1 0.989 against 0.987, rg2 0.014 against 0.016, load-balancer 0.578 against 0.587. Two re-admission routes explain it. `stage_restore_elites` appends elites after the whole filter chain (issue #73), and, far wider, `stage_select` pools all of ctx.m_parents unfiltered under NSGA-II (mu+lambda) at include/genetic/pipeline.hpp:402. Moving elitism ahead of the filters would not fix this: parent pooling is 100% of the population against elitism's 10%.
results.criteria: Pre-registered criterion 1, soundness, was written as the campaign's gate and it fails. final-only leaks at 0.427 against every-gen's 0.000, so the two arms are not comparable on quality or yield: final-only buys its repairs by emitting ones the filter would have rejected. Criteria 2 (quality non-inferiority) and 3 (yield) are therefore void as the plan specified, and the reported result is the leak itself. Criterion 4, cost, is not the deciding figure once criterion 1 has failed. The stepping-stone hypothesis does not survive: final-only's apparent advantage on arbiter in the pilot is the artefact the plan named as a live threat, not the effect it hypothesised.
results.result_2_filtering_is_cheaper_than_not_f: every-gen's median paired wall ratio against the unfiltered control is 0.949. A candidate dropped before the scoring stage never costs a model-count or a synthesis query, and that saving exceeds what the filter's own ltlsynt calls cost. This removes the cost argument the filter was held off by default for.
results.result_3_yield_loss_is_an_artefact: every-gen's found_repair is 10 points below the unfiltered arms, 0.899 against 0.999, but found_repair counts a run as successful whether or not its repairs are well-separated. Counting instead the runs that emitted at least one well-separated repair reverses the ranking: every-gen 2158/2400 = 0.899, nofilter 2051/2400 = 0.855, final-only 2057/2400 = 0.857. every-gen is the best arm on yield once yield is measured on output the filter would accept. It also carries the highest implies_ideal, 0.355 against 0.315, with 152 discordant pairs gained against 57 lost versus the control. The nominal loss sits in exactly two of the sixteen specs, both at implies_ideal = 0.00 in every arm. rg1: found_repair falls from 1.00 to 0.39, yet well-separated yield rises from 5/150 to 58/150, and its unfiltered leak rate of 0.987 says nearly everything the filter removes there was output the filter is meant to remove. arbiter: found_repair falls from 1.00 to 0.00 and well-separated yield falls from 33/150 to 0/150, against an unfiltered leak rate of 0.905. Every other spec holds found_repair at about 1.00 under every-gen.

caveats: arbiter is a real regression and is not explained away. Filtering every generation takes it from 33/150 to 0/150 on well-separated yield, and it is the pilot observation that motivated the campaign. This is a separate claim from the one criteria retires: what the leak refutes is final-only's apparent advantage, which was re-admitted output rather than search; what stands is that every-gen genuinely loses arbiter against the unfiltered control. A stepping-stone effect is the obvious reading of that one spec, and rg1 refutes it as a general one -- there the same filter improves well-separated yield elevenfold.
Only intervals 1 and 1000 are on the grid, so nothing here says whether some intermediate cadence beats both ends.

every-gen leaked once in 9529 repairs, detector seed 18 repair_2.tlsf. A final well-separation gate, matching what the weakening and vacuity filters already have, is still worth adding. Issues #72 (stage_filter_fallback re-admits the whole unfiltered offspring set when the chain empties the population), #74 (a realizability timeout is read as well-separated and cached for the rest of the run, material at ltlsynt_timeout_ms = 500) and #77 (the seed population is never filtered) each describe a route this campaign did not close.

The leak rates are over emitted repairs, not runs, so a spec that emits many repairs per run weighs more heavily in the pooled figure than one that emits few. The per-spec breakdown is the one to read.
TLSF only. Well-separation is measured inert on the FRETISH path, where assumptions are input-only in practice, and this campaign says nothing about it there.

The vendored copy deliberately keeps the text that ran, so the two blobs differ by that comment alone.

merge_experiments.py.basis: recorded: verbatim from the commit that ran the campaign.

It was staged to /tmp on both hosts and ran there; both hosts' copies still hash to this blob, checked after the campaign closed. This is the script behind every leak figure above.

av2's startup manifest, carrying the recorded binary version

closing: The campaign set out to price a schedule and ended up measuring a leak, because the arm that was supposed to filter once never filtered at all. What survives is a filter that is cheaper to run every generation than to skip, and one spec that still loses everything when it does.
